title: Routed experts split between the device and the CPU tier, in the device's bits
description: heterogeneous-expert-dispatch's partition. Host form: routes whose expert the expert_residency slot holds on the device run there (at most device_slots of them), the rest on the host; each route's weighted contribution is accepted into async-expert-contributions' ContributionGroup, which settles a token only when every route's receipt is done and sums them in route order, so the output is bitwise the reference whichever side ran a route. Device form on CUDA: nvfp4 / int4 experts; routes whose slot is -2 computed by host-expert-tier's CPU tier, posted and joined inside the stream through one of the host's handoffs (Core's crit_plugins.host; one post and one join a layer, capturable), the others by the device part, summed in route order; both parts in host-expert-arithmetic's declared integer block order, so the split never changes a bit.

resident.description: forward() over the plugin's own store: the experts of each layer kept on the device (the lowest ids; -1 all); the others go to the CPU tier

max_tokens.description: the most tokens one post sends the CPU (a decode step or verify round; the handoff's slot holds this many tokens of the model's top routes); a longer call posts in pieces

join.description: how the stream waits for the CPU: auto takes the cheaper capturable join the host measured on the device (crit_plugins.host)

native.description: the CPU tier's rows: native (built at load) or the declared order in torch; without the native tier CPU routes are joined on the host, outside capture

workers.description: the workers of the host's pool (Core's, crit_plugins.host: one a process) when this plugin is the first to ask for it (-1: Core's plan, one per physical core but the service thread's)

pin.description: with workers: pin each worker of the host's pool to a physical core of its own (Linux)

rows_per_task.description: rows of one expert in a CPU pool task

device_part.description: the device part's rows: auto, crit's grouped-experts kernel in the declared order where it builds and reads the tier's bundles as they are, else DeclaredRoutes in torch (one route at a time, exact, slow); kernel refuses to load without it; torch always runs DeclaredRoutes. Both give the CPU tier's bits

prompt_arithmetic.description: the arithmetic of a call past max_tokens (prompt chunks) that sends no route to the CPU: auto (the default), tensor where the engine's configuration asks repeatable prompt rows (exactness, docs/PLUGINS.md#exactness) and the kernel device part is here, declared otherwise; declared, the CPU tier's integer order like every other call; tensor, the grouped-experts kernel's BF16 tensor cores (W4A4 for nvfp4 bundles), much faster, other bits than decode rows: a prompt scores its tokens a little apart from the replies decode serves, which a speed engine's honesty bound allows and a preserve engine's exact one does not. Needs the kernel device part

kernels.name: cpu-routes
kernels.fallback: the host path: the CPU tier served outside the stream, a synchronization a layer (not capture-safe)

kernels.name: grouped-experts
kernels.fallback: DeclaredRoutes: the declared order in torch, one route at a time (exact, slow)
